request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

A: The iteration silently changed failure semantics for the pre-existing path: the console.error zodError logging was removed and the code now throws via parseRefreshTokenResponse on schema failure, ungated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Existing self-hosters who never enable credential sync lose the previous graceful behavior (log and continue with stale-but-usable credentials) and instead get a thrown error on any malformed Microsoft token response — an objective change smuggled into the sync PR without being called out for acceptance.
B: The removed console.error block means a failed token parse now surfaces only the context-free 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with neither the zod issue nor the Microsoft response logged. When the new minimum-schema or provider-schema parse rejects a real Microsoft response, on-call debugging has no record of what the provider returned, misdirecting investigation of Outlook token failures introduced by this diff.

PAIR 9:
A: The sync-mode fetch has no timeout, status check, or error handling, and the endpoint URL/env-var gating is duplicated as the same two-condition check in both refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse. When the sync endpoint is slow or down, every calendar operation hangs on an unbounded fetch (calendar reads are on the booking hot path); and the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` pair is hand-maintained in multiple files, so the next sync-aware call site can easily enable only one half of the mode.
B: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortSignal, making it a timeout-less outbound call on the token-refresh path which executes inside user-facing booking and calendar operations. A hung or slow sync endpoint stalls each affected calendar operation for the platform's default connect/idle timeouts (undici: minutes), piling up concurrent booking requests and worker capacity on a dependency that is not on any critical provider's SLA.
